operating_notes.text: Bank of Maharashtra reported 394 fraud cases involving ₹990.00 crore during FY26.
IBU (GIFT City) loan book stands at INR8,200 crores, built in 8-9 months
Refinance borrowing of INR19,000 crores at blended cost of 6-6.5% used to fund credit growth
Branch expansion at 200 branches annually supports deposit and advance growth
GIFT City IBU book stands at ₹8,200 Cr with USD 965 million of sanctions, contributing 3% of the 27% advances growth.
Refinance borrowing of about ₹19,000 Cr at a blended cost of 6-6.5% brings the CD ratio down to 81.99% from 86% domestic.
Gold loan book grew 75% YoY to ₹13,000 Cr; ECLGS sanctions of ₹4,500 Cr against a ₹6,700 Cr eligible portfolio, with ₹3,560 Cr disbursed.
CASA deposits were 48.44% of total deposits as on June 30, 2026, down from 52.51% as on March 31, 2026.
Cost of interest-bearing funds rose to 4.44% in Q1FY27 from 4.36% in FY26, versus PSB average of 4.94% in FY26.
Branch network stood at 2,815 as on June 30, 2026, with about 41% in Maharashtra.
Fitch rates the USD 500 million MTN programme BBB-, at the bank's Long-Term IDR, which is equalised with India's sovereign BBB-/Stable on a 73.6% government stake.
Fitch assigns BB(xgs) to the MTN programme, aligned with the bank's bb Viability Rating.
Fitch ESG score of '4' for Governance Structure, citing board independence and ownership concentration as negative for the credit profile.
S&P Global Ratings assigned BBB to Bank of Maharashtra's USD 500 million EMTN programme on 7 September 2026, equalising with the issuer credit rating (BBB/Stable/A-2).
Jun-26 global credit-deposit ratio 88.82%, up from 83.28% at Mar-26 and 66.85% at Mar-22.
Top three funded sectors are Infrastructure 17.73%, Housing 16.99% and Agriculture & Allied 13.65%, together over 48% of funded exposure.
Yield on advances 8.57% and cost of deposits 4.38% at Jun-26, both annualised.
Fitch rates the USD 500 million notes at the same level as BOM's Long-Term IDR, which is equalised with India's sovereign IDR of BBB-/Stable.
Reversed COVID-19 contingency provisions of ₹250 Cr during Q2FY27; holds balance provision of ₹510 Cr as on Sep 30, 2026.
Total business crossed ₹7 lakh crore as of September 2026.
Corporate proposal pipeline stands at ₹23,000 Cr, with ~₹10,000 Cr expected to be disbursed by March 2027.
Total gold loan outstanding reached ₹33,000 Cr, of which agri gold loan is ₹18,600 Cr and MSME gold loan is ₹2,000 Cr.
Received ₹1,200 Cr under Maharashtra debt waiver up to Sep 30, with an additional ₹115 Cr received on Oct 1; remaining ~₹1,500 Cr targeted by March 31, 2027.

timeline.summary: Q4FY26 results (consolidated): interest earned ₹7,755.18 Cr (+15.2% YoY), net profit ₹2,044.88 Cr (+36.1% YoY).
Bank of Maharashtra reported Q4FY26 net profit of ₹2,014 crore, up 34.89% YoY, with gross NPA improving to 1.45%.
Bank of Maharashtra’s Board, led by Vishal Sethia, recommended a final dividend of Rs. 1.20 per equity share (12%) for FY2025-26, adding to the interim dividend of Rs. 1.00.
Bank of Maharashtra’s **Vishal Sethia** hosted an earnings conference call for Q4FY26 and FY26 on **2026-04-20**, with recording available at the bank’s website.
Bank of Maharashtra reported FY26 net profit of ₹7,019 Cr up 27% YoY, with gross NPA improving to 1.45%.
Bank of Maharashtra’s promoter, the President of India, held 73.60% equity shares as of March 31, 2026, with no encumbrance declared for FY 2025-26.
Bank of Maharashtra reported Q1FY27 results with 27% YoY net profit growth and 27% YoY advances growth.
Bank of Maharashtra's Q1FY27 earnings call reaffirmed 18% FY27 loan growth and 3.75% NIM guidance after 27% advances growth, with the ₹5,000 Cr equity raise still awaiting government approval.
On 21 July 2026, ICRA reaffirmed AA+ (Stable) on Bank of Maharashtra's ₹12,000 Cr Basel III Tier II and infrastructure bonds, citing GNPA of 1.45% and CET I of 15.56% as of June 30, 2026.
Chief Compliance Officer Uma Vedula resigned effective 23 July 2026 for personal reasons; the Bank is appointing a new CCO at CGM level from its existing pool.
Bank of Maharashtra established a USD 500 million Euro Medium Term Note Programme on 05 September 2026
On 7 September 2026, Fitch assigned BBB- to Bank of Maharashtra's USD 500 million EMTN programme, equalised with its sovereign-linked BBB-/Stable IDR, and BB(xgs) on an ex-government support basis.
On 7 September 2026, S&P Global Ratings assigned BBB to Bank of Maharashtra's USD 500 million EMTN programme, equalising with its issuer credit rating.
On 7 September 2026, Bank of Maharashtra released a September 2026 investor presentation showing Jun-26 global advances of ₹3,059.64 bn, GNPA 1.45%, NIM 3.79% and CASA down to 48.51%.
Bank of Maharashtra priced $500 million MTN notes at 6.112% p.a. on September 17, 2026
On 21 September 2026, S&P Global Ratings assigned a BBB rating to Bank of Maharashtra's USD 500 million MTN notes issued under its medium-term note programme.
On 23 September 2026, Bank of Maharashtra notified of a proposed bank strike on 28-30 September 2026.

On 24 September 2026, Fitch Ratings assigned a final BBB- rating to Bank of Maharashtra's USD 500 million 6.112% senior unsecured notes due September 2031, the same as the expected rating of 17 September 2026.
Chief Vigilance Officer Shri Amit Srivastava superannuated effective 30 September 2026
On 01 October 2026, Bank of Maharashtra appointed Shri Devdatta Rokade as Chief Compliance Officer.
Q2FY27 results (consolidated): interest earned ₹8,606.39 Cr (+20.7% YoY), net profit ₹2,136.48 Cr (+28.0% YoY).
Bank of Maharashtra reported Q2FY27 net profit of ₹2,310 Cr, up 41.42% YoY.
In its Q2FY27 concall, Bank of Maharashtra confirmed strong credit growth exceeding its 18% target, RoA above 2%, and voluntary ECL provisioning of ₹500 Cr.
Bank of Maharashtra revised its Marginal Cost of Funds Based Lending Rate (MCLR) across tenors effective October 31, 2026.
